To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the generalization properties of DNNs are intimately tied to the geometry of the optimization landscape and to the nature of the loss function.

(a) for linear classifiers in binary classification, the minimization of the logistic loss, the cross-entropoy loss and the exp-loss leads to asymptotic convergence to the maximum-margin solution, and (b) for multilayer neural networks (MLNNs) with nonlinear activations, the minimization (with gradient descent) of the exponential-type loss functions leads to asymptotic, “slower than linear”, convergence to minimum norm solutions.
